You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:

# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the source item near the center still identifiable as the same DVD in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass if an edited object can be confidently matched to the source item and remains identifiable as a DVD. Fail if a confidently matched object is no longer identifiable as a DVD. Unknown if the source item's DVD identity or its correspondence to an edited object cannot be determined. Do not infer identity solely from an edited object being a white disc.
node.binding: Assess the source's small printed rectangular item near the center and compare it with edited objects by position, shape, and scene context. The source item need not be unmistakably labeled a DVD, but uncertainty about its label alone is not a reason for unknown if correspondence and DVD identity are otherwise visually supported. Do not treat either nearby white disc as the same DVD without supporting correspondence.

node_traces.evidence: The source item near the center is a small printed rectangular object. It is absent from the edited image, which instead shows two white discs; neither can be confidently matched to the rectangular item by position, shape, or scene context. The source item's DVD identity and correspondence to an edited object therefore cannot be established.

response.content: {"text":"The binding’s “small printed rectangular item” description conflicts with the source image: the item near center appears to be a DVD case/package, while the requested object is the black DVD. This misbinding makes the node assess the wrong object and drives an unjustified unknown. Anchor the comparison to the black disc in the source and evaluate whether that same disc was changed to white in the edited image, using spatial/contextual correspondence and visible appearance; do not require the printed package itself to match either edited disc. Keep unknown only if correspondence genuinely cannot be established. The trace is a valid visual uncertainty, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure; the reference “no” is aggregate guidance, not proof of an atomic label."}
